thread:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER: CRITICAL - Multiple containers in gpu-pool-east-3 entering CrashLoopBackOff (segfault). Pod template: runtime-engine:v2.1.4. Affected nodes: node-gpu-17,node-gpu-18.

alex (oncall): acked. I'm on it. tagging @maria for runtime logs / kernel traces.

maria (eng-runtime): grabbing logs now. first glance: repeated SIGSEGV inside fused attention kernel. stack shows something in custom_quant_kernels.cu.

alex (oncall): any OOMs or GPU driver messages?

maria (eng-runtime): here's the tail from one pod:

```
I0315 21:12:02.123456 1 runtime_server.cc:412] starting
E0315 21:12:04.789012 1 fused_kernel.cu:1024] CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered (700)
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what():  Segmentation fault (core dumped)
#0  0x7f8a2e93 in custom_quant::apply(..) at fused_kernel.cu:1024
#1  0x7f8a2b00 in runtime::execute_layer(..) at runtime_engine.cc:887
#2  0x7f8a1f11 in inference_loop(..) at server_main.cc:451
```

No clear OOM lines, but CUDA illegal memory access suggests out-of-bounds in the kernel.

karen (support): customer impact: two customers routing inference to this pool see 5-10% error rate, one big customer (acme-media) reports high latency and 500s.

alex (oncall): thanks @karen. Maria - can we isolate whether this is model-specific (a particular model shard) or hardware-specific? Any pattern across nodes?

maria (eng-runtime): pattern: crash pods are on both node-gpu-17 and node-gpu-18, same model version redwood/gpt-quant-v2. Crash happens when sequence length > 1024 in production traffic. We see KV cache path used heavily.

sre-bot: Deploy: rolling-deploy/runtime-engine:v2.1.3 -> v2.1.4 detected 3414509800 by ci-cd-bot.

alex (oncall): rollback candidate? v2.1.3 was stable right?

maria (eng-runtime): yes v2.1.3 had no crashes for this workload. We can roll back but need to mitigate customer traffic first. Proposed steps: 1) scale down affected pool and move traffic to backup pool (cpu-fallback or smaller-gpu pool), 2) cordon node-gpu-17/18, 3) roll back runtime to v2.1.3 on that pool, 4) collect full core dumps and backtrace for root cause.

devon (next-oncall): I'll take the handoff once we have a stable rollback. stepping in to run node cordon/evacuate.

alex (oncall): timeline? do we need a Pager escalation to SEs?

maria (eng-runtime): ETA for rollback + traffic shift: ~12-18 minutes if infra approves ephemeral capacity. I want to collect core dumps before restart if possible. Please enable core dump collection on affected nodes (gcore, preserve /var/crash).

karen (support): I'll message account team for acme-media and notify them of mitigation steps. Current impact: ~8% of inference requests for them hit 500.

alex (oncall): infra - @devon, can you spin up a small backup-gpu pool (2x A10) and shift 30% traffic? Use routing policy 'graceful-fallback' in console.

devon (next-oncall): doing it now:
```
kubectl scale deployment runtime-pool-backup --replicas=2 -n prod
# await nodes to warm cache
```

10m later...

devon (next-oncall): backup pool ready, routing rule applied. shifting traffic 30% -> backup-gpu. monitoring logs.

maria (eng-runtime): rolling runtime rollback on gpu-pool-east-3 to v2.1.3. command: `kubectl set image ds/runtime-engine runtime-engine=redwood/runtime-engine:v2.1.3 -n prod`

sre-bot: Note: do not restart pods on node-gpu-17 until core dump is collected.

alex (oncall): confirmed. Maria, please attach gdb backtrace to the incident convo when you have it.

maria (eng-runtime): grabbed a core from one crashed container, minimal backtrace:
```
#0 0x00007f8a2e93 in custom_quant::apply(float*, int, ..) at fused_kernel.cu:1011
#1 0x00007f8a2b00 in runtime::execute_layer at runtime_engine.cc:887
#2 0x7f8a1f11 in inference_loop at server_main.cc:451
```
Looks like indexing with sequence length calculation produced index overflow in quant kernel. Sending tarball to /tmp/inc-3414509876/coredumps.tar.gz and uploading to S3 s3://redwood-incidents/3414509876/coredumps.tar.gz

karen (support): I told acme-media rep we have mitigations in place and they acknowledged. They asked for postmortem.

alex (oncall): Good. Any remaining crash pods after rollback?

maria (eng-runtime): after rollback to v2.1.3, crashloops dropped to zero on those nodes. New pods are healthy. CPU-fallback handled lower-priority customers.

devon (next-oncall): nodes still cordoned, scheduling draining for maintenance window. Will uncordon after we finish artifact collection and hotfix.

alex (oncall): OK, handing off to @devon for follow-up (postmortem and final customer comms). @maria please open a bug with reproducer and link to coredump + stack trace. Add regression test for long-sequence quant path.

devon (next-oncall): taking over. I'll create incident ticket INC-3414509876, assign to eng-runtime, and schedule hotpatch window.

sre-bot: Incident INC-3414509876 created, severity P1 -> Owner: devon.

alex (oncall): thanks everyone. Closing active pager. Please add any additional notes here.

maria (eng-runtime): note: likely root cause = sequence-length calculation mismatch after an internal refactor to KV cache indexing in v2.1.4. Repro steps included in ticket. Will prioritize patch.

karen (support): noted. Will follow up with acme-media with timeline for postmortem.

devon (next-oncall): will continue mitigation and coordinate hotfix with eng-runtime. Handoff complete. :thumbsup:
